doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Toronto's pop music, Luigi Romanelli and her older brother
summary: No real music scene in Toronto; her older brother and his college friends taught her the instruments.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So the music in Toronto, when you were growing up, was the typical pop music of the times?
Luigi Romanelli was like the Lombardos.
And then, but I had an older brother that Duke was also very fond of. And he and I would listen and go to things together. And so that way, he and his friends who were going on to
college, they trained me you know, and they were beginning to play something. And they’d say, “Well that’s a clarinet you know.” And I would tell them, “That’s what’s good.”
